result.topic_en: Euler computes the variation of the integral ∫Z dx: he writes δZ in terms of δy and its derivatives, replaces δy by an arbitrary infinitesimal ω, and integrates by parts to separate an integral part (giving the Euler–Lagrange expression N − dP/dx + ddQ/dx² − …) from boundary terms.
result.transcription:
106 DE METHODO

Hincque ergo variatio functionis Z pro quouis ipsius $x$ valore definiri poterit; quae forma adhuc magis illustrabitur, si, quemadmodum est $dZ=Mdx+Ndy+Pdp+Qdq+Rdr$ etc. obferuetur, esse oportere, ob $\delta x=0$,
$\delta Z=N\delta y+P\delta p+Q\delta q+R\delta r+$ etc.
tum vero esse, ob $p=\frac{dy}{dx}$, $q=\frac{dp}{dx}$, $r=\frac{dq}{dx}$ etc.
$\delta p=\frac{\delta dy}{dx}=\frac{d\delta y}{dx}$; $\delta q=\frac{\delta dp}{dx}=\frac{d\delta p}{dx}=\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}$; $\delta r=\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3}$.
XX.
Cum ergo translatione in statum variatum functio Z incrementum capiat $\delta Z$, ipsa formula $\int Z dx$ incrementum nanciscetur $\int\delta Z\,dx$, quod itaque erit:
$\int dx(N\delta y+P\frac{d\delta y}{dx}+Q\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}+R\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3}+$ etc.)
in quo, si post integrationem ponatur $x=a$, obtinebitur variatio ipsius A, seu $\delta A$, quae nihilo aequalis posita inducet quantitati A valorem maximum seu minimum. In hac autem integratione non amplius ad transitum in statum variatum respicitur, sed ea per omnia incrementa ipsius $x$ extendi debet, cum denotet summam omnium variationum singulis valoribus ipsius $x$ a termino $x=0$ vsque ad $x=a$ conuenientium. Ne igitur ratio differentialium per $\delta$ indicatorum turbet, pro $\delta y$ scribatur $\omega$, ita vt $\omega$ exhibeat quantitatem infinite paruam arbitrariam vtcunque ab $x$ pendentem; ac superius incrementum nihilo aequandum erit:
$\int dx(N\omega+P\frac{d\omega}{dx}+Q\frac{dd\omega}{dx^2}+R\frac{d^3\omega}{dx^3}+$ etc.)
XXI.
Perspicuum est, in his differentialibus superioribus elementum $dx$ assumi constans; quia enim posuimus


MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 107

mus $\frac{d\delta p}{dx}$ seu $d.\frac{\delta p}{dx}=\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}$, ob $\delta p=\frac{d\delta y}{dx}$, aperte $dx$ constans est assumtum. Hoc ergo obseruato, si singulas partes integralis inuenti seorsim integremus, habebimus:
$\int dx.N\omega=\int N\omega dx$
$\int dx.P\frac{d\omega}{dx}=\int Pd\omega=P\omega-\int\omega dP$
$\int dx.Q\frac{dd\omega}{dx^2}=\int\frac{Qdd\omega}{dx}=\frac{Qd\omega}{dx}-\frac{\omega dQ}{dx}+\int\frac{\omega ddQ}{dx}$
$\int dx.R\frac{d^3\omega}{dx^3}=\int\frac{Rd^3\omega}{dx^2}=\frac{Rdd\omega}{dx^2}-\frac{dRd\omega}{dx^2}+\frac{\omega ddR}{dx^2}-\int\frac{\omega d^3R}{dx^2}$
etc.
Hinc itaque variatio quaesita partim ex membris integralibus, partim ex absolutis constabit, eritque:
$\int\omega dx(N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+$ etc.)
$+\omega(P-\frac{dQ}{dx}+\frac{ddR}{dx^2}-$ etc.$)+\frac{d\omega}{dx}(Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+$ etc.)
$+\frac{dd\omega}{dx^2}(R-$ etc.)
XXII.
Restituamus $\delta y$ pro $\omega$, ac formulae integralis $\int Zdx$, existente $dZ=Mdx+Ndy+Pdp+Qdq+Rdr+Sds$ etc. et $p=\frac{dy}{dx}$; $q=\frac{dp}{dx}$; $r=\frac{dq}{dx}$; $s=\frac{dr}{dx}$ etc. incrementum, dum in statum quemcunque variatum transfertur, quod hoc modo $\delta\int Zdx$ exprimere licet, ita se habebit:
$\int dx\delta y(N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-$ etc.)
$+\delta y(P-\frac{dQ}{dx}+\frac{ddR}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3S}{dx^3}+$ etc.)
$+\frac{d\delta y}{dx}(Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+\frac{ddS}{dx^2}-$ etc.)
$+\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}(R-\frac{dS}{dx}+$ etc.$)+\frac{d^3\delta y}{dx^3}(S-$ etc.)

items.quote: si post integrationem ponatur $x=a$, obtinebitur variatio ipsius A, seu $\delta A$, quae nihilo aequalis posita inducet quantitati A valorem maximum seu minimum
items.english: If after integration x=a is put, the variation of A, i.e. δA, is obtained, which, set equal to zero, gives A a maximum or minimum value.

items.quote: Perspicuum est, in his differentialibus superioribus elementum $dx$ assumi constans
items.english: It is evident that in these higher differentials the element dx is taken as constant.

items.quote: Hinc itaque variatio quaesita partim ex membris integralibus, partim ex absolutis constabit
items.english: Hence the sought variation will consist partly of integral terms and partly of absolute (boundary) terms.
